rv.q: And as it embarks on its third London run, it again proves to be merely decent. The songs are good but the book falls between two stools: it pays cosy tribute to the brilliant 1975 film ‘Monty Python and the Holy GraiI’, but half-heartedly tries to become a satirical musical about putting on a musical.

Spamalot was always an inane musical extravaganza, or the best ever medieval pantomime, depending on your satirical mind-set, and it’s decisively the latter in this slick and pretty scaled-down version directed by Christopher Luscombe and smartly designed – in classic panto style – by Hugh Durrant .
Monty Python's Spamalot Book and lyrics by Eric Idle, music by John Du Prez and Eric Idle Playhouse Theatre, London From 14 November 2012.
If you want to laugh, laugh some more and perhaps even sing-along to ‘Always Look On The Bright Side Of Life’ then you must clear your diary and book tickets to see Spamalot.
Even those who are usually adverse to musicals should see this show, it might just change their minds.
If you haven't seen this show then you really are missing out on a treat.

cn.t: This irreverent Monty Python musical delivers silly, lighthearted fun that satirizes both Arthurian legend and musical theatre itself, though critics find the show merely decent, with its dual satirical strands never quite gelling into a cohesive whole.
